textbookText: 3. Absorption of nutients: Absorption is that process by which the digested food is passed into blood stream. It occurs either by active transport or by passive transport. Absorption is mainly carried out in the duodenum and ileum as their inner layer is very much suited i.e. modified as absorptive surface or villi (singular; villus). Each villus is richly supplied with blood capillaries and lymph vessel or lacteal. Water, mineral salts and other nutrients are passively absorbed through the mucosa. The amino acids, glucose and fructose are absorbed by the diffusion through mucosa and passed into the blood capillaries and finally reach the liver through the hepatic portal vein. The glycerol and fatty acids pass into lymph vessels called lacteals. The glycerol can be absorbed easily as it is soluble in water, whereas the fatty acids cannot be absorbed as they are insoluble in water. So, before absorption the fatty acids mix with bile salts to make themselves water soluble substance called micelles. The micelles now enter intestinal mucosa cell where they are converted to chylomicrons which enter to lymph ducts or lacteals.

4. Assimilation: Assimilation is the process in which absorbed nutrients are utilized by the body. Nutrients are utilized by body as per need such as synthesizing enzymes, amino acid, repairing cells and tissues, stored as reserve food material for future use, running metabolic activities etc. Similarly, Glucose is transported by the blood into the cells and tissues where glucose burns with oxygen or oxidizes to release energy, carbon dioxide and water.

5. Egestion of undigested Food: After the completion of digestion and absorption in small intestine, undigested food enters rectum by peristalsis for storage and formation of faeces. Undigested food particles, old epithelial cells, leucocytes, bile pigments and large number of bacteria forms faecal matters which are discharged through the cloacal aperture.
